conventions: Resumption in relative clauses. Where the ASV writes a single pronominal adverb for the relative and its resumptive, they share one unit headed on the relative: asher + sham -> wherein (12.2), asher + sham + directive he -> whither (12.29, three morphemes, one word). Where the clause carries a further resumptive the ASV does not write - b-o at 12.11 and 12.18, where sham has already taken the there, and otam at 12.2, where the antecedent is the object - that morpheme is its own unrepresented unit under rule 22's first sentence. Both shapes occur in this chapter and the BSB disagreements at 12.11, 12.18 are this convention, not errors.

pen is rendered by the discontinuous that ... not (12.13, 12.19, 12.30 twice) and kept in one unit headed on not, since the negation is what distinguishes the pair from a bare complementizer, as rule 35 heads a Nor on its negative. Heading on that is the competing reading and is named in each verse note; the chapter was not checked against corpus precedent for this lemma.

mishlach yad recast as a relative clause (12.7, 12.18). The whole recast frame - that ye put ... unto, that thou puttest ... unto, including the supplied subject pronoun and the stranded unto - belongs to mishlach and heads on the lexical verb, discontinuous under rule 25; yad keeps hand and its suffix the possessive. Nothing else in the clause answers for the unto.

kol with a relative is fused only where the ASV spends one word on the pair: 12.32's What ... soever is one unit on kol plus asher, with davar keeping thing and its article unrepresented because the determination is inside that word. Where the ASV writes a word for each, rule 2 splits them and kol keeps whatever generic the ASV supplies to complete it: 12.8's all the things goes to kol, headed on all under rule 31, and that goes to asher.

Comparative particles are counted against the morphemes present. 12.15 writes ke twice and each takes its own as of, with the assimilated article taking the written the; 12.16 and 12.24 write no the, so the assimilated article is unrepresented. 12.22 writes kaasher once and the ASV rewrites as over the coordinated member, so both occurrences belong to that one morpheme's discontinuous unit under rule 25 and the second is not added.

Rule 31 heads in this chapter's offering and servant vocabulary. olah, terumah and nedavah head on the modifier (burnt, heave, freewill), as do pasil (graven images) and qodesh (holy things), because the ASV never writes the generic noun alone for those words. eved, amah and tirosh head on the class noun (servant, servant, wine), because the ASV writes that noun alone for words of the same class, which is rule 31's tie-break rather than a different convention.
report: Read all 32 verses end to end against the 60-lemma candidate table. Every multi-treatment bucket resolves to a difference the ASV actually writes and the source licenses; no construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the Hebrew to account for it. No patches.

Resumptives were where a split could hide, and they hold. asher+sham fused as wherein (12.2) and asher+shammah fused as whither (12.29) meet rule 30's one-English-word condition, because that word carries the relation and the resumption together; 12.11 and 12.18 write which and a separate there for sham, so the further resumptive b-o is genuinely unwritten under rule 22's first sentence, and 12.2's otam goes the same way. One convention applied twice each way, not two conventions.

Comparative counts hold in both directions: 12.15 writes ke twice and each takes its own as of; 12.22 writes kaasher once and the ASV rewrites as over the coordinated member, so both occurrences are that one morpheme's discontinuous unit under rule 25 rather than an added word. The chapter has zero added units, and reading the dump end to end I found no supplied English that should have been one. The supplied to of 12.11 (to the place) is rule 33's directional adverbial accusative, the to your mountain case, and not rule 16's topicalizing as for; the verse note says so.

Rule 31 head placement is consistent and correctly discriminated. The three offering compounds head on the modifier (burnt, heave, freewill), following rule 31's own olah example, as do graven images and holy things; man servant, maid servant and new wine head on the class noun, because the ASV writes that noun alone for words of the same class. Both readings stand in one chapter by rule 31's own test, not by drift.

Possessive clauses are divided by which morpheme is present, exactly as rule 43 directs: 12.12 is verbless, so the lamed takes hath, its suffix takes he and ayin takes no; 12.26 writes hayah, so the verb takes hast, the lamed is unrepresented, and the suffix takes thou, which the ASV writes beside the relative's which.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. Sn x6 is rule 32; R x11 is rules 27, 40 and 52 (lemor's lamed, dative lamed before a bare English object, and the lamed before the modal's bare complement at 12.17); Td x9 is rules 12, 41 and 47 (assimilated article with no written the, and articles silent where a demonstrative carries the phrase's one determiner). The three singleton disagreements are the same conventions: the resumptive suffixes at 12.11 and 12.18, and hu at 12.23, where rule 20 puts the supplied is on the predicate nephesh and leaves the copular pronoun unrepresented. That last is the closest call in the chapter; the verse note already names the competing reading, and I have not touched it to move an aggregate.

No promotions or amendments. The two candidates were pen rendered that ... not (12.13, 12.19, 12.30 twice, headed on not) and le-bilti plus infinitive at 12.23 (lamed takes that, bilti takes not, the infinitive takes thou eat). Both already follow from the contract by composition - rule 35's reasoning that the negation is what distinguishes the fused word from a bare connective, and rules 48 and 52 read together - and no corpus precedent for either lemma was supplied here, so promoting would be writing a rule the corpus might contradict. Recorded as conventions instead.
